limitations: Experimental scheduling only. No engine physics, shaders, constants, or existing source files are changed. No physical acceptance or sustained display-rate claim follows from this harness.
Baseline routes to the exact original frame body and uses no timestamp feature, GPU wrappers, or host CPU profiles by default. Private source adds read-only native timing and observer access.
Limit1 and limit2 admit complete original-order machine frames when native queue-prefix fences have capacity. Skipped RAFs retain elapsed time as host debt and submit no machine render.

Capacity bounds machine frame bundles, not all native commands. Existing outside-frame UI draws and asynchronous instruments remain intact; their fences can exceed the nominal limit. Raw foreign counts and observed frame-bundle bound status are required. A strict native command-depth bound is never certified.

GPU callbacks only release capacity or advance completion frontiers. Input release is immediate; catch-up uses live current input, never a saved held action. Packet cadence can still change frame-count-based behavior and coupling.

Pause, visibility loss, and not-ready suspension retain debt but exclude paused wall time. Reset cancels old-scene debt explicitly and guards old completions. Device or queue failure pauses the private candidate.

The native 0.05-second clamp and fixed-step overflow shedding exist in ordinary sources. Safe packet size considers native accumulator, maximum substeps, pending quiet-water bank, and jello budget; observed native input accounting also runs when fixed stepping is off.

A quiet-water bank beyond safe capacity pauses with an error rather than claiming its elapsed time was preserved. Empty or inactive native work can produce unaccounted simulation time; that metric is evidence, not an assertion of loss cause.

Submitted native clock is a CPU submission frontier. Completed-prefix clock is sampled queue-prefix completion, not current presented state. Mirror-applied clock is a sparse CPU snapshot frontier and can lag completed GPU work.

Scaled clock rates use nominal instrument units. None is an exact completed physical playback rate. Post-drain frontiers are separate; draining does not force the paused CPU mirror to apply a later readback.

Read-only native timing audit counters measure dt clamp, ignored calls, fixed-bank overflow and nonfixed maximum-substep hits. Nonfixed cap hits stretch substep dt and do not by themselves discard simulation time.
Required uncapped Chrome flags measure scheduling throughput, not hardware refresh FPS. Accepted machine frames and observed RAF callbacks are separate rates.

GPU_PROFILE=1 requests timestamp-query before device creation, wraps native APIs and host functions, and adds sampled query tail copies. CPU encoder time is not GPU time; profile overhead and pool drops remain disclosed.

No per-frame await occurs in the hot loop. Prefix promise creation/delivery and telemetry still have overhead. Baseline prefix observation is sparse at QUEUE_SAMPLE_MS; completion-rate precision differs between variants.
If GPU capacity is below incoming elapsed-time rate, host debt grows. Bounding GPU work moves backlog to an explicit host bank and does not itself establish real-time 60 FPS.
